A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with a high risk of thromboembolisms should have their warfarin withheld for a short period of time.

the use of an In- Office Point-of-Care international normalized ratio measuring device in the office setting can be a very useful tool for the safe management of the antithrombotic patient undergoing routine oral and maxillo-facial surgery.

the use of an INR monitoring device can be a valuable tool to safely simplify the perioperative management for the oral and maxillo-facial surgeon of the anticoagu-lated patient and make the management more efficient for the surgeon and patient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients on warfarins are not at risk for bleeding when undergoing minor oral surgery.
patients on warfarins who require “minor” oral surgery can safely maintain their anticoagulation and not require discontinuation of their medication.
oral and maxillo-facial surgery can safely be performed on patients on warfarins.
